{"summary":"I reviewed only the supplied deltas, the two new test files and trusted-entry-rate-limit.ts. The import swaps in the 20 routes are mechanical and keep the original limits and keys. The new GET limiter on /api/live-interactions (1200/min in its own "live-interactions-read" bucket) runs before validation and before any database access. Its capacity math holds for GET-only polling: 32 viewers × 30 polls plus 32 initial reads is 992 per minute. The client backoff applies Retry-After on 429/503 for both GET and the scripted POST, and the abort cleanup is covered by tests.

One MAJOR issue remains. While a scripted event is active, every 2-second poll also sends a POST {action:"open"}, and POSTs are still capped at 60/min per trusted source. That breaks the stated 32-viewer shared-IP target at 3 or more viewers. Because of the new early return on POST 429/503, the GET refresh is skipped during backoff, so those viewers' whole interaction panel stops updating.

There is also one MINOR issue: Retry-After is only capped at the browser timer maximum, about 24.8 days. A bad header value could therefore stop polling for the rest of the session.

Scope proposal, not a defect: the other per-viewer polled endpoints (live-danmaku GET at 120, cards GET at 120, playback-source at 120, presenter GET at 60) now also count against one trusted source IP. Their client polling rates weren't supplied, so I couldn't check them against the 32-viewer target. That should be a separate scoped review.

Not certified: the whole WP (8 raw action/helper callers and the existing identity callers remain), the commercial Upstash/Vercel-native evidence, and deployment readiness. An empty or short findings list doesn't certify that tests or a release pass.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","file":"src/components/live-advanced-interactions.tsx","area":"refresh(): scripted interactionRequest({action:"open"}) per poll + new 429/503 early return (~lines 165-182); POST limit in src/app/api/live-interactions/route.ts","issue":"While a scripted event is active, the polling loop sends a POST every 2 seconds. That POST still uses the 60/min per-source limit, so the 32-viewer shared-IP target fails during scripted events. The new backoff also skips the GET, which freezes manual interactions and spotlight updates too.","evidence":"refresh() calls interactionRequest({ action: "open", vendorId, liveId, eventId }) on every cycle whenever scriptedEvent is set, so each viewer sends about 30 POSTs per minute. The test matrix confirms POST /api/live-interactions is limited at 60 per trusted source. The new capacity test only exercises GET. With 3 or more viewers behind one trusted IP (CGNAT, corporate NAT, classroom), the POST bucket runs out within the first minute. The new branch `if (status 429||503) { retryDelay = error.retryDelay; return; }` then skips the GET fetch, so setRun/setSpotlight don't update for the Retry-After period, and this repeats every window.","impact":"Shared-IP audiences, the exact case the follow-up targets, lose scripted interactions and also manual runs and spotlight updates for most of every minute during scripted events. The 32-viewer capacity contract therefore holds only when no scripted event is active.","recommended_fix":"Stop polling the mutating open POST. Call open once per eventId (or have the GET return scripted-run state) and use the read bucket for steady-state polling. Alternatively, give scripted open its own bucket sized for 32 × 30/min plus headroom. When the POST is backed off, still run the GET, or back off only the POST, so that manual interactions and spotlight keep refreshing.","required_test":"Add a capacity test that simulates 32 trusted viewers on one source for 60 seconds with an active scripted event (POST open + GET every 2 seconds) and asserts that no 429 is returned. Add a component test showing that a scripted POST 429 does not suppress GET refresh of manual runs and spotlight, or update the existing test if the intended contract changes.","confidence":0.72},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/components/live-advanced-interactions.tsx","area":"interactionRetryDelay upper clamp (~lines 45-52)","issue":"Retry-After is capped only at the setTimeout maximum (2,147,483,647 ms, about 24.8 days), so one oversized header can stop polling for the rest of the session.","evidence":"The tests assert that "9999999999" maps to 2_147_483_647. The repo's own limiter returns delays within one window (60 s here), but any 429/503 from an intermediary (CDN or WAF) with a large Retry-After or a far-future date stops all interaction updates and gives the viewer no signal.","impact":"A misconfigured or hostile intermediary can silently disable the interaction panel until the viewer reloads.","recommended_fix":"Cap the delay at a small product-defined maximum (for example 60–300 s, tied to the limiter window), and update the overflow test to assert that cap.","required_test":"Unit test that a very large Retry-After value and a far-future date both clamp to the chosen maximum.","confidence":0.5}]}
